stories.headline: US Readies Tariff Hike on China, EU Goods as Soon as Tuesday
stories.summary:
The Trump administration is preparing to announce as soon as Tuesday night a new round of tariffs on goods from China, the European Union and more than a dozen other economies, according to people familiar with the matter. The move is meant to replace levies that were struck down by the Supreme Court. The U.S. trade representative's office is expected to unveil the plan.

The EU, Japan and South Korea are expected to face tariffs of 15% or less, while China, India and Vietnam could face higher rates. The new levies would cover most imports and would likely be added to existing tariffs of 10% to 12.5%. Final rates remain subject to change before the announcement.

The action would reshape U.S. trade policy after the court ruling and affects trading partners across Europe and Asia. It comes as Washington and Beijing try to reach a trade deal ahead of an expected December meeting between President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping. Supporters of tariffs say they protect domestic industry and give Washington leverage in negotiations, while critics argue they raise costs for consumers and businesses and invite retaliation. Details and final rates are expected once the trade representative's office releases its plan.

stories.headline: Update: Attorney General Blanche Declines to Say Whether Nvidia Is Under Investigation
stories.summary:
U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche backed Nvidia as a "good corporate citizen" on Tuesday while refusing to say whether the chipmaker or its CEO is under federal investigation. Asked several times whether the Justice Department or FBI had investigated Jensen Huang, Blanche replied: "I don't know what you're talking about." He said he had no information about Huang's security clearance status.

Huang was reinstated by Nvidia's board on Monday, less than two weeks after he resigned over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy who led Megaspeed, a Singapore-based Nvidia customer. President Trump said he spoke to the directors and convinced them to bring Huang back. The board said it had received input from senior levels of the U.S. government and was confident Huang posed no national security risk. The Commerce Department is preparing to blacklist Megaspeed over suspected chip diversion to China, and the Commerce and Justice departments said they began investigating the firm in 2024 for potential export control violations.

Blanche said the Justice Department has "hundreds, if not more" export investigations at any one time. The reinstatement drew bipartisan anger, with Republican Rep. Don Bacon among the critics, and Huang is due to testify before Congress next week. Nvidia shares fell more than 7% in early afternoon trading Tuesday, though they remained well above Friday's close. Chinese state media has called the spy allegations a smear campaign, and Beijing is watching the episode closely as chip export rules remain a sticking point in trade talks.

stories.headline: Car Bomb Wounds More Than 20 in Colombian City of Villavicencio
stories.summary:
A car bomb exploded Monday evening in front of the regional government offices in Villavicencio, a city in central Colombia, injuring at least 23 people and damaging several buildings. No group has claimed responsibility. The attack is the latest in a series of bombings targeting official buildings and security forces' headquarters.

President Abelardo de la Espriella blamed "narcoterrorism" and promised to respond "bluntly and forcefully" to "every drop of Colombian blood spilled," adding that there would be no impunity and no retreat. Earlier Monday, drones dropped explosives on the police headquarters in Cucuta. Three weeks ago, three adults and a baby were killed in a car bomb attack near army barracks in Tolima province. Armed groups appear to have stepped up attacks in retaliation for an offensive De la Espriella ordered against them.

The bombing came on the eve of the 10th anniversary of the 2016 peace deal with the FARC. De la Espriella has called that agreement a "false peace" and a waste of public resources, while its signatories, former President Juan Manuel Santos and Rodrigo Londono, defend it. Violence has risen in recent years as FARC dissident factions and criminal groups fight over drug trafficking, illegal mining and extortion. Former President Gustavo Petro's "total peace" talks with armed groups collapsed after several groups violated ceasefires.

stories.headline: Huawei Convicted of Trade Secret Theft and Bank Fraud, Acquitted of Racketeering
stories.summary:
A U.S. federal jury found Huawei guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud, but not guilty of the more serious overarching racketeering charge, following a two-month trial. Federal prosecutors first announced charges against the Chinese technology and telecommunications giant in 2019.

Prosecutors argued Huawei spent 20 years doing whatever it took to gain a competitive edge, including lying to banks about its business dealings in Iran and stealing technology secrets from rivals. Assistant U.S. Attorney Meredith Arfa made that case in closing arguments. The defense, led by attorney Brian Heberlig, argued that prosecutors had decided Huawei was a criminal organization and built their case from there, and said the company's growth, with operations in 170 countries and more than 200,000 employees, came from its own innovation.

Huawei said the racketeering acquittal "confirms that these allegations lack factual basis and vindicates our consistent position over the past eight years." The verdict lands amid heightened U.S.-China tension over technology, including chip export controls and trade talks ahead of an expected December meeting between President Trump and Xi Jinping.

stories.headline: Trump, Putin and Xi Issue 'Joint Declaration on Peace' After Talks in China
stories.summary:
President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping issued a "joint declaration on peace" after roughly 90 minutes of talks in China, in what the BBC described as a historic trilateral meeting. The BBC's analysis characterized the summit as high on spectacle and short on substance, with few concrete commitments detailed so far.

The meeting is a major diplomatic moment for Xi, who hosted the leaders as China showcases its technological ambitions. BBC coverage noted it also carries pitfalls for Beijing, including questions about what China gains from bringing the leaders together and how the declaration will translate into policy on the war in Ukraine and other disputes.

The summit coincides with fallout from Nvidia's reinstatement of Jensen Huang as chief executive, which analysts say bears on U.S.-China technology competition. The BBC commentary suggested Huang's return is no guarantee of relief for Beijing on chip export restrictions, though the article text provided gives limited detail on specific outcomes.

Observers will be watching for whether the declaration produces any follow-up on Ukraine, trade or technology controls. Supporters of direct engagement argue that talks among the three powers are necessary to reduce tensions, while skeptics say a declaration without enforcement mechanisms changes little on the ground.

stories.headline: Trump Awards Rudy Giuliani the Presidential Medal of Freedom
stories.summary:
President Donald Trump presented former New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani with the Presidential Medal of Freedom, the nation's highest civilian honor, in the Oval Office on Tuesday. The White House praised Giuliani's leadership after the September 11, 2001, attacks, when he became known as "America's Mayor," and a White House official called him one of the greatest leaders in the country.

The award comes more than a year after Trump announced plans to bestow it. Giuliani, 82, said on Steve Bannon's "War Room" podcast on Monday that the presentation was coming. He later served as Trump's personal attorney.

The honor is politically charged. Critics note that Giuliani was disbarred for his efforts to help Trump overturn the 2020 election results, and outlets such as The Guardian emphasized that record. Supporters, including Trump allies and right-leaning outlets, point to his post-9/11 leadership and decades of public service as justification for the award.

stories.headline: Israeli Air Strike Kills Hamas Internal Security Chief in Gaza
stories.summary:
An Israeli air strike in western Gaza City killed Naeem Abu Nahel, head of Hamas's internal security service, according to Gaza's Hamas-run interior ministry. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz announced he had been "eliminated." At least seven Palestinians were killed in Israeli strikes across Gaza, according to health officials and first responders.

Witnesses said a drone targeted the 50-year-old as he walked near a tent camp for displaced people. He had held the post only since September, when his predecessor was captured by Israeli special forces. The Israeli military said he advanced attacks on Israeli troops and civilians and that his death was a blow to the apparatus's management capabilities.

Six others died in two earlier strikes, including three at a police station in al-Mawasi. Gaza's police said two of its officers were among the dead and accused Israel of a campaign targeting the police apparatus. Israel said it struck military operatives.

Violence has continued despite the US-brokered ceasefire agreed in October last year. Gaza's health ministry says at least 1,679 people have been killed in the past 13 months, while Israel says six soldiers have died. The UN has urged Israel to allow in more supplies ahead of winter.

stories.headline: Houthi Attack on Riyadh Financial District Tower Injures 11
stories.summary:
Saudi authorities said the Houthis injured 11 people in an attack on a tower in Riyadh's main business district. Two Saudi nationals and nine foreigners were hurt, according to the Saudi-led anti-Houthi coalition.

The strike is a further setback to the kingdom's efforts to establish its capital as a global financial center, a central goal of its economic diversification plans. The attack targeted the financial hub that hosts many international firms and workers.

It comes amid wider regional tension involving Iran, whose allies include the Houthis. Further details on the weapon used and any Saudi response were not immediately available.

stories.headline: Airline Glitches, Coastal Storms and Soaring Fares Threaten Thanksgiving Travel
stories.summary:
Americans are heading into the busiest travel week of the year after a series of airline system failures, a forecast of storms on both coasts and sharply higher airfares. The Federal Aviation Administration's network malfunction recently set off the longest nationwide ground stop in 25 years. Last week, United Airlines and Delta Air Lines each suffered their own outages, producing hundreds of delays.

Delta said its operations were stable Monday, a day after more than 1,000 of its flights were delayed when an automated system that calculates aircraft weight malfunctioned. "Delta teams are focused on keeping the operation moving safely and caring for our customers," the airline said. Roundtrip domestic tickets for Thanksgiving were up more than one-third from a year earlier, according to Hopper estimates made in late October.

The National Weather Service expects rain on the East and West coasts and dry conditions in the middle of the country. Heavy rain and high winds are forecast to begin Wednesday night along the Carolinas coast, reach the New York City area on Thanksgiving Day and arrive in Maine by Friday. Moderate to major coastal flooding is forecast from Washington state to Southern California because of possible record king tides.

The wind forecast has raised questions about the balloons in the 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade. City law bars full-size balloons if sustained winds exceed 23 mph or gusts top 35 mph. Forecasters expect the rain to hold off until after the parade ends, but wind remains a concern.

stories.headline: Update: Seattle Airport Operator 'Outraged' After ICE Arrests Two Passengers Boarding Flight
stories.summary:
Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers arrested a father and daughter as they boarded an Alaska Airlines flight to Los Angeles at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport on Saturday morning. ICE said the two, Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza and Sofia Hernandez Mejia, are Mexican nationals arrested for allegedly overstaying their visas. The Port of Seattle, which runs the airport, said it was "outraged" by the incident.

ICE said that during the man's arrest, "other travellers began to obstruct and assault our law enforcement officers," calling that a federal crime and a felony. It said the woman "hurled hot coffee on the officers" and would be charged with assaulting a federal officer. The pair's lawyer, Olia Catala, said the two had no criminal history, were in a legal process and were traveling to a family baptism, and that the officers' unmarked jackets caused panic and chaos.

A fellow passenger, John Gaedeke, told Reuters the agents did not identify themselves before tackling a man, and that he did not see anyone throw coffee. Alaska Airlines said it was not given appropriate notice of the enforcement action and is concerned about the distress it caused. The Port said immigration actions at the airport happen without its knowledge and that it is asking the Department of Homeland Security whether agreed protocols were breached.

The arrests add to the debate over immigration enforcement in public places. Critics, including Washington's governor, have condemned the operation, while the administration maintains it is enforcing federal immigration law and protecting its officers.

stories.headline: Russian Governor of Murmansk Region Detained in Rare Corruption Case
stories.summary:
Andrei Chibis, the 47-year-old governor of Russia's northern Murmansk region, has been arrested on corruption charges. It is the first detention of a regional leader in five years. He was reportedly taken in for questioning on arrival in Moscow on Monday.

He is suspected of embezzling more than a billion roubles (about $12.2 million) set aside to build an Arctic highway, plus a further 39 million roubles from the regional construction budget. Reports say investigators allege a criminal group was set up in 2022 to siphon regional funds and move them abroad, including to Kyrgyzstan. Chibis denies wrongdoing, and his wife called the accusations "ridiculous."

The case is notable because Chibis is considered an active supporter of Russia's invasion of Ukraine, and no regional governor had been arrested since the war began, even as many high-ranking officials were. Murmansk is a key military location in the Arctic and hosts the Northern Fleet. The UK and EU have sanctioned him over alleged involvement in transporting Ukrainian children to Russia. A court is to decide Wednesday whether he stays in custody, according to Interfax.

stories.headline: UK Sanctions Five Myanmar Military Leaders After ICJ Genocide Ruling
stories.summary:
The United Kingdom has sanctioned five senior Myanmar military leaders after the International Court of Justice ruled that the country committed genocide against the Rohingya minority, the first time a state has been found guilty of the crime. The sanctioned officers are Myo Htut Hlaing, Myo Min Tun, Myat Thet Oo, Kyaw Soe and Kyaw Swar Oo. Australia, Belgium, Portugal, Spain and Canada have also acknowledged the ruling.

Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said a response to genocide "must reflect our values and must be matched by clear action." He confirmed new legislation to halt aviation fuel supplies to Myanmar and said the UK would raise the issue at the UN Security Council this week, with a dedicated meeting in a fortnight. Last week he expelled Myanmar's defence attache.

The court ruled by nine votes to six that genocidal intent was the only reasonable inference from the evidence, and found about 10,000 Rohingya were killed in the 2017 operation in Rakhine state. More than 700,000 Rohingya fled to Bangladesh in that campaign. Myanmar denies the claims. Miliband also called for a pause in hostilities, an end to air strikes on civilians and the release of political prisoners.

stories.headline: Update: White House Asks Congress for Billions in Added Funding in Stopgap Spending Bill
stories.summary:
The White House sent Congress a 12-page list of "anomalies" on Monday night, outlining exceptions to current spending levels that it wants included in any stopgap bill lawmakers take up next month to keep federal agencies funded. The request, first reported by Politico, would allow the administration to spend billions of dollars more than current funding levels in certain areas.

The request lands as lawmakers approach a government funding deadline in early December. House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries has declined to rule out a government shutdown to advance his party's agenda, citing the appropriations process before the Dec. 11 deadline. Democrats will take control of the House in January with a large majority, which gives the stopgap negotiations added political weight.

The anomalies list is a routine tool in short-term funding fights, since continuing resolutions otherwise freeze spending at prior-year levels. How many of the requested increases Congress accepts will shape the scope of the stopgap and how much leverage each party holds. Lawmakers are expected to take up the measure after the Thanksgiving recess, and the details of the White House's priorities are likely to draw scrutiny from both parties.

stories.headline: Update: Iran Says No Talks With US Until Its Seven Conditions Are Met
stories.summary:
Iran said it will not negotiate with the United States on ending the conflict until seven conditions it has set are met, according to Associated Press reporting on Tuesday. The statement hardens Tehran's public position as tensions persist over the U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports and incidents in the Strait of Hormuz.

Qatar's prime minister said he is working to de-escalate tensions between Iran and the United States. Iranian officials have said they would use all available means to end the blockade, which they call an act of military aggression. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has said the strait could reopen if Washington meets Tehran's demands.

The Iranian stance follows recent reports that President Trump said he is inclined to strike Iran after the new year if no deal is reached. The U.S. has also been reported to have delayed a possible strike as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu pressed for a joint offensive. Qatari mediation is now the main visible diplomatic channel, and the open question is whether either side will soften its position before the year-end timeline Trump has signaled.

stories.headline: Appeals Court Moves Trump Hush Money Case Toward Federal Court
stories.summary:
A federal appeals panel handed President Trump a win on Monday in his effort to overturn his New York hush money conviction, ruling that a lower court wrongly denied his bid to move the case into federal court. The 2nd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals found that a federal judge erred in concluding Trump had waited too long to raise his presidential immunity defense.

The decision sends the case to federal court, where Trump could seek dismissal of the charges on immunity grounds. It could also clear the way for him to argue that prosecutors relied on evidence protected by presidential immunity. The ruling is described as his biggest legal victory yet in his efforts to move the case out of New York's state courts.

The ruling does not by itself erase the conviction, and further proceedings will determine whether the immunity arguments succeed. Supporters of the president have long called the case politically motivated, while critics argue the conviction should stand because it concerned private conduct before he took office. Prosecutors may seek further review of the panel's decision.

stories.headline: Russian Drone Violates Polish Airspace During Strikes on Ukraine
stories.summary:
A Russian drone violated Polish airspace late Monday night during Moscow's latest wave of long-range strikes on Ukraine, the Polish military said. The drone briefly strayed into Poland during a nighttime attack on western Ukraine.

The incident came just days after three Russian missiles crashed in Poland, raising concern among NATO members about spillover from the war. NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte has warned that Russia's war machine is running at full speed and could threaten Europe long after the fighting in Ukraine ends.

The airspace violation adds to a widening pattern of incidents along NATO's eastern flank. Russian officials, meanwhile, have issued nuclear warnings, with former President Dmitry Medvedev saying Moscow could consider a preventive nuclear attack in certain circumstances. Poland's response and any NATO consultations will be watched closely.
